opportunities.title: Small grants

deadlines.raw: 31 March for a decision in May
15 September for a decision in November
15 December for a decision in March
28 February for a decision in April
30 September for a decision in November

amount.raw: Awards vary but will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 and will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000. Up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days; up to £2,500 per person for 14+ days; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more; Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD students.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects, though the UK office may consider individuals with organisational support. Awards not made to undergraduate or master's students.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding enabling UK-Japan projects that bring people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, encourage exchange of ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language and cultural studies, and academic research/visits.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December, for a decision in March of the following year

amount.raw: Butterfield Awards of up to £10,000; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally show an existing research record, but consideration is given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Preference to those who have not previously been involved in UK-Japan collaboration; early-career applicants particularly welcomed. Project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Grants may be used for travel expenses, conference and publication costs.
